newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Taiwan defence minister visits Prague.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan defence minister visits Prague.

text.p: Taiwan's Defence Minister Chiang Chung-ling was in the Czech Republic, the Taipei Business Chamber said on Tuesday, in the latest in a series of top-level Taipei contacts even though Prague only recognises China.
The visit has been shrouded in secrecy and came amid Czech media reports an aerospace industry deal was in the offing.

"The minister arrived on Sunday for two or three days," an official at the chamber, which represents Taiwanese interests in the Czech Republic, told Reuters. The official, who asked not to be identified, declined to give further details.
The Czech Foreign Ministry said last week that Chiang arrived on Friday. A ministry spokesman revised this on Tuesday to say the visit had begun on Sunday.

"Because it is a purely private visit, and the minister is not meeting any officials, we really do not know his programme," the ministry spokesman said. "We know about the visit only because of the visa he needed."

The Czech Republic, once part of the former Communist state Czechoslovakia, does not have diplomatic relations with Taiwan. But Prague defends the country's right to do business with the the state, which China regards as a renegade province.
The Czech media have reported Taiwan was interested in cooperating with troubled aircraft maker Aero Vodochody, which makes military trainers, albeit to build small business jets.

Last year Beijing reacted angrily when Taiwanese Premier Lien Chan visited the Czech Republic for a private, but highly-publicised visit, in which he met President Vaclav Havel and Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus for talks.
Havel also irritated China by expressing regret that Taiwan was not a member of the United Nations.

Taiwanese Economics Minister Chiang Pin-kung visited Prague last year, announcing a $100 million industrial park would be opened in the western city of Plzen this year. So far nothing has materialised.
Relations with Beijing improved in April this year when Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen visited Prague.
